title: SQLAlchemy and Alembic for those not using Django

videos.script: Until now, the API kept its events in a dictionary. Restart it, and they are back as they were. Start four copies, and each one has its own. {{title}} Today the API gets a database. FastAPI brings none of its own, so you add the one most Python projects use: SQLAlchemy. {{engine}} You write two classes, and SQLAlchemy prints the tables they describe. {{models}} Alembic turns that into a migration. You read the file before you run it. And then you rename a column, and watch Alembic get it wrong. {{rename}} It saw one column removed and another added. On a table with rows, that migration failed. On an empty one, it would have dropped your data without a word. {{fix}} Then the same query problem as lesson 4, in a new library. Four queries for three events, and then two. {{queries}} Last, the race. Twenty people, twelve seats, four worker processes. Without a lock, eighteen to twenty got in. A lock in Python cannot help, because there are four Pythons. {{race}} The lock that works is a row lock in PostgreSQL. With it, twelve got in, every time.
